title: High-probability rank growth conjecture for generalized Moore matrices
statement:
Let $\bm{M} \in \mathbb{F}_{q^m}^{k \times n}$ be a randomly chosen matrix with full $\mathbb{F}_{q^m}$-rank such that each block $\bm{M}^{(i)}$, for $i=1,\dots,\ell$, has full column rank over $\mathbb{F}_q$. Let $\bm{a} \in \mathbb{F}_{q^m}^{\ell}$ consist of randomly chosen representatives of distinct nontrivial conjugacy classes of $\mathbb{F}_{q^m}$, and fix $j \in \{1,\dots,n-k\}$. **High-probability rank growth conjecture.** The iterated operator $\Gamma_{\bm{a}}^j$ satisfies

$$
\operatorname{rk}_{q^m}(\Gamma_{\bm{a}}^j(\bm{M}))=\min((j+1)k,n)
$$

with high probability. This claim is analogous to an assumption used for Overbeck's distinguisher and contrasts with the deterministic rank growth of generalized linearized Reed–Solomon codes; establishing the probability of this behavior for random full-rank matrices is the relevant issue.
source_name: Felicitas Hörmann, Hannes Bartz and Anna-Lena Horlemann, “Distinguishing and Recovering Generalized Linearized Reed-Solomon Codes”, arXiv:2304.00627 (2023).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.00627

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2023).
